chunks.arabic_text: ٨ - إِدْرِيسُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، يُكْنَى أَبَا الْفَضْلِ، الْكَفْرَثُوثَائِيُّ، خُوزِيّ الْأَمِّ. يَرْوِي عَنِ الضُّعَفَاءِ.

translations.en: 8 – Idrīs ibn Ziyād, known by the kunya Abū al-Faḍl, al-Kafarthawthā’ī. Khūzī on his mother’s side. Narrates from weak narrators.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Idrīs ibn Ziyād al-Kufrathutha'i as a narrator of moderate standing who primarily transmits from weaker sources, a detail crucial for assessing the reliability of chains containing his reports. His specific nisbah and maternal lineage help distinguish him from other narrators with similar names in the complex landscape of Shia hadith criticism.
en.seo_question: Who is Idrīs ibn Ziyād in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.أَبُو الْفَضْلِ: Abū al-Faḍl, the kunya (teknonym) of the narrator
key_terms.الْكَفْرَثُوثَائِيُّ: Al-Kafarthawthā’ī, a nisbah indicating origin or association
